audit.whatIsWrong: Not one of Zaahen's five abilities is named anywhere in either layer. The full layer uses the literal placeholder word "Ultimate" as if it were the ability name — "- Zaahen Ultimate: matchup-defining", "Track Zaahen's Ultimate before you commit", "Zaahen wastes Ultimate", "Engage only on Ultimate's cooldown".
audit.why: The packet carries enemyAbilities: null for this matchup, so the generator fell back to a placeholder — but champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json is complete and on disk. The result is the emptiest entry in my slice: 71 matchups' worth of template with no opponent in it. Every instruction is un-followable because the player is told to track an ability with no name, no cooldown and no tell.
audit.corrected: P Cultivation of War (Determination stacks, bonus AD, revive at full). Q The Darkin Glaive 10/9/8/7/6s, double slash, heals, recast knocks up, auto-reset. W Dreaded Return 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, 850 range, pulls. E Aureate Rush 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s dash. R Grim Deliverance 110/95/80s, heals.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere warns that Aureate Rush scales with the target's maximum health.
audit.why: This is the most important single fact in the matchup and it is absent. Tahm Kench's entire build and his whole kit are max-health-based — Heartsteel, grey health conversion, the passive's bonus damage from total health. Aureate Rush is flagged percentHealth: "punishes HP stacking — armour alone is not the answer", which means the more Tahm Kench commits to his own scaling the harder that dash hits him. The existing text says the opposite, promising a "near-unkillable brick" at two items.
audit.corrected: Aureate Rush scales off your max health, so raw HP stacking feeds it — you need resistances alongside the Heartsteel, not instead of them.

audit.whatIsWrong: The displacement race is never mentioned, despite both champions carrying knockups.
audit.why: The missing-interactions file flags this matchup explicitly: both sides carry displacement — Abyssal Dive against The Darkin Glaive's recast knockup and Dreaded Return's 850-range pull — and whoever lands it first owns the trade. For a Tahm Kench whose engage IS a knockup, knowing that his opponent can pull him out of position from 850 range every 14s is the difference between initiating and being initiated on.
audit.corrected: Dreaded Return pulls from 850 range every 14s. Abyssal Dive is your knockup. First displacement wins the trade.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid and whys[4] describe Tahm Kench's own ultimate as "a map tool rather than a fight-winner" and "a roam tool".
audit.why: Tahm Kench's R is Devour — he eats a champion. It is the single most fight-deciding button in his kit and it has no map function whatsoever. This looks like the same underlying confusion with the removed pre-2020 Abyssal Voyage that I found across the rest of this slice, surfacing here as a description rather than a name. Telling a player his level-6 spike is a roam tool means he never uses it in the duel it wins.
audit.corrected: Devour is the fight-winner at 6. There is no map tool in the kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early says "his stun and sustain tools are not online yet", and the same sentence then uses "his" for what the parallel line in whys[1] calls "your" tools.
audit.why: Two problems in one clause. The pronoun is wrong — whys[1] shows the sentence is describing Tahm Kench's own stun and sustain — and more importantly Zaahen has no stun at all. His crowd control is the knockup on The Darkin Glaive's recast and the pull on Dreaded Return. A player braced for a stun that does not exist will misread every early trade.
audit.corrected: Zaahen has no stun. His CC is the Darkin Glaive recast knockup and the Dreaded Return pull.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: zero cooldown-sequencing advice. breakdown.cooldowns says "His big cooldown. Trade around it" without naming it or numbering it.
audit.why: The tracked cooldown was also the wrong one. Grim Deliverance at 110/95/80s is a long ultimate, but the ability that governs every lane trade is Aureate Rush at 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s — it is how he enters and how he leaves, and the seconds it is down are the only time a Tahm Kench with three stacks can actually catch him. Dreaded Return at 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s is the second window.
audit.corrected: Step in when Aureate Rush is down (10s at rank 1). Dreaded Return 14s, Grim Deliverance 110s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is never mentioned, and neither is the passive revive.
audit.why: Both The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance heal him, which is exactly the pattern Grievous Wounds exists for, and the matchup is flagged needs-antiheal. Separately, Cultivation of War lets a fully-stacked Zaahen REVIVE — that changes all-in maths completely, because a won fight can un-win itself. Neither fact appears anywhere.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal his Q and R. A full Determination bar gives him bonus AD and a revive, so a fight you won may not be over.

edits.before: Levels 1 and 2 are honest farming — his stun and sustain tools are not online yet and neither is your full kit. Level 3 changes it: Tongue Lash stun and Thick Skin sustain arrive together and hand you the trade game. Stack Q passively, absorb his aggression, and let 4-5 pass even.
edits.after: Levels 1 and 2 are honest farming — Zaahen has no stun at all, only the Darkin Glaive knockup on its recast. Level 3 hands you the trade game. Stack An Acquired Taste, absorb his aggression, and remember that Aureate Rush deals percent health, so Heartsteel alone will not save you.

edits.before: At 6 a close duel is a wash despite your R being a map tool rather than a fight-winner — his all-in is real but your grey health refuses to let it finish. From your first item the tilt is permanent: Thick Skin shielding out-sustains his trades, and every exchange leaves you healthier than him.
edits.after: At 6 your R is Devour, a fight-winner and not a map tool — three stacks removes him outright. Watch the displacement race: Abyssal Dive knocks up, his Q recast knocks up and Dreaded Return pulls from 850 every 14s, and whoever lands it first owns the trade. Grim Deliverance heals him too.

edits.before: At two-plus items you are a near-unkillable brick who simply wins the 1v1 — his burst finds no threshold and his sustain cannot race yours. Sit on the carry he wants, stun his engage, and soak the damage that was supposed to kill somebody. He needs picks; you make picks impossible.
edits.after: At two-plus items you are a near-unkillable brick, with one caveat: Aureate Rush scales off your max health, so stacking HP alone feeds it. Cultivation of War also lets a fully-stacked Zaahen revive, so a won fight is not always over. Sit on his target and soak the burst.

notes: ROOT CAUSE worth fixing upstream: the packet carries enemyAbilities: null for zaahen, so the generator substituted the literal string "Ultimate" wherever an ability name belonged and produced the emptiest entry in the slice — no Zaahen ability is named anywhere in either layer. champ-data/_kits/zaahen.json is complete and on disk, so the packet builder and the content generator are reading different sources. Any other matchup with enemyAbilities: null will have the same placeholder text and is worth grepping for (search the content and full files for the bare word "Ultimate" used as a name). Two facts I added are the ones that actually change how this lane is played: Aureate Rush scales with the target's MAX HEALTH, which directly punishes Tahm Kench's own Heartsteel/grey-health scaling and contradicts the old "near-unkillable brick" line; and Cultivation of War lets a fully-stacked Zaahen revive, so a won all-in can reverse.
